chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: Jabo Smith and the Jenkins Orphanage Band
summary: Budd describes Jabo Smith's trumpet and trombone talent, and the orphanage band that marched to raise funds.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Then after he ate he would have to take a little nap. Well by that time, after he woke up, then he would come up and start playing. Well it was almost time for the other bands to get off from their jobs, and they used to come by and hear this combo, and especially to hear Jabo Smith play. And he would wake up, and this cat would blow so much trumpet, he had so much talent it wasn't even funny.

And he could also play an awful lot of trombone. I don't know whether very many people ever heard him play the trombone, but he was great on the trombone, playing jazz. And he told me that when he was in the Jenkins Orphan Home Band that he did a lot of trombone playing, but he finally found out that they needed a solo trumpet, so he used to be the solo trumpet in the Jenkins Orphan Home Band.
And there he gained an awful lot of experience. The guy could triple tongue, double tongue, single tongue, do everything, played the -- he could play a beautiful legit
trumpet, and he was a great story teller. He was always trying to write stories, and very interesting.
You're right You write about that. You (Inaudible). He sure did do that, didn't he?
Yeah, he was great. He was a great, great, great player, and a great guy. And --
There were some other guys out of that -- famous musician out there, out of that Jenkins Home. Who else was out of that Jenkins Orphans Home? Remember?
You know, maybe Tommy Young played with that band at one time. I think I remember him telling me that. But they turned out some great musicians, because --

-- I remember when I was a kid, they used to parade like through the streets, you know, to raise money, and would have a great big American flag, and the band would be playing, and kids would be carrying the American flag, and people would be throwing dimes, nickles, quarters, pennies, out there, at the orchestra, and everything, into this great big flag. The flag was almost as wide as the street itself. And they had permission to go to different cities and march through the town, then that helped raise funds for this Orphan home.
